name: Knee bounce
summary: Soft knees that dip a little on each beat. Almost every other move sits on top of this.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft
On each beat, let your knees dip a few centimetres
Come back up between beats, but never lock your knees
Let your shoulders and head ride along with the bounce
tips: Find the kick drum first and bounce only on that
Smaller is cooler: a tiny bounce on time beats a big one off time
mistakes: Bouncing up on the beat instead of down
Locking the knees between bounces, which makes it look stiff
why: Feeling the beat in your knees is what makes the rest of your body look like it's dancing to the music rather than next to it.

name: Step-touch
summary: Step to one side, bring the other foot in to tap, then go back the other way.
steps: Step your right foot out to the right (1)
Bring your left foot in and tap it next to the right (2)
Step your left foot out to the left (3)
Tap the right foot next to it (4)
tips: Keep the knee bounce going underneath
Once it's automatic, let your shoulders swing the opposite way to your feet
mistakes: Stepping too wide, which eats floor space and pulls you off the beat

name: Weight-shift sway
summary: Feet stay put while your weight rolls from one foot to the other, and the hips follow.
steps: Feet a bit wider than hip-width, knees soft
Shift your weight over the left foot on 1, so the right heel can lift
Shift over the right foot on 2
Let the hips and shoulders follow the weight, not lead it
tips: Try it at half speed (one shift every two beats) for slow tracks
This is the move to fall back on when you've lost the beat
mistakes: Swinging only the hips while the weight stays in the middle

name: Loose arms
summary: Give your hands somewhere to be: elbows bent, hands around waist to chest height, moving with the body.
steps: Bend your elbows and bring your hands up to between waist and chest
Loosen your fists, or make them soft
Let the hands rise and fall a little with the knee bounce
Every few bars, change it: one arm swings, or both hands push down on the beat
tips: Watch the hands of someone whose dancing you like, then borrow one gesture
mistakes: Arms hanging straight down, which reads as 'not dancing'
Arms flying wide on a crowded floor
why: Most people feel awkward because of their arms, not their feet. A default arm position takes that worry away.

name: Dancing in a crowd
summary: Keep your moves inside your own footprint, and go bigger only when there's space.
steps: Before you start, notice how much room you have around you
On a packed floor, keep feet under your hips and elbows in
Save spins, kicks and wide arms for when a gap opens
If you bump someone, a quick smile or hand on the heart is all it takes
tips: Face the DJ or the speakers when it's packed: everyone moves the same way and nobody collides
mistakes: Practising a big new move in the middle of a packed floor
why: Being easy to dance next to is the fastest way to feel welcome on any floor.

name: Half-time drift
counts: Step on 1, hold 2 · step on 3, hold 4
summary: Slow, gliding steps on every other beat, as if you were walking through water.
steps: Step slowly to the side, or a little forward, on 1
Let the other foot follow and settle on 2, no rush
Step the other way on 3, settle on 4
Keep the upper body tall and let the head turn slowly with the steps
tips: Roll through the whole foot when you step, heel to toe or toe to heel
Close your eyes for a few bars to stop yourself rushing
mistakes: Stepping on every beat, which turns it into a march
why: Dancing in half time is what makes goth dancing look effortless, even at a club tempo.

name: Cobweb hands
summary: Hands slowly push and part the air in front of you, as if you were clearing away cobwebs.
steps: Bring both hands up in front of your face, palms out
Over two beats, sweep one hand slowly out and down to the side
Over the next two, the other hand follows on its own path
Let the wrists lead and the fingers trail behind
tips: Change levels: high above the head, then low by the hips
Your eyes can follow one hand, which adds a lot of drama for free
mistakes: Moving both arms the same way at the same time, which looks mechanical

name: Slow turn
summary: A small, unhurried turn on the spot in tiny steps, with the arms trailing.
steps: Turn your head and shoulders a little first to start the turn
Take tiny steps on the spot in that direction, one every two beats
Finish facing the front after 8 beats
Let one arm float out behind you as you turn
tips: Pick a spot on the wall and find it again at the end, so you don't get dizzy
Turn the other way next time, so both sides get practice
mistakes: Spinning on one foot, which is fast and needs much more space

name: Stomp march
counts: Right on 1 · left on 2 · right on 3 · left on 4
summary: March on the spot, putting each foot down flat and heavy, right on the kick drum.
steps: Lift your right knee a little and stamp the foot down flat on 1
Same with the left on 2
Keep the knees soft as you land, so the stomp goes into the floor and not your joints
Lean the upper body slightly forward
tips: Hit harder on 1 than on the other beats
Wear boots you can stomp in. Barefoot practice at home is fine, just softer
mistakes: Landing with a straight leg, which jars the knees

name: EBM two-step
summary: One foot steps forward and back on the spot while the arms pump, switching feet every few bars.
steps: Step your right foot forward and put weight on it (1)
Step it back to where it started (2)
Repeat on 3 and 4
Pump the opposite arm forward and back with the foot, fists loose
After two or four bars, switch to the left foot
tips: Lean into the forward step a little, as if pushing through a crowd
Add a small heel stomp on the back step
mistakes: Taking big steps: this move lives in a small square on the floor
why: It's the move you see on almost every EBM floor. Once you have it, you can fit in anywhere industrial is playing.

name: Punch and pull
counts: Punch on 1 and 3, pull on 2 and 4
summary: Alternate fists punch down or forward on the beat and pull back, like working a machine.
steps: Fists up at chest height, elbows bent
Drive the right fist down and forward on 1
Pull it back sharply on 2
Left fist on 3, back on 4, while the feet keep the stomp march going
tips: Keep the punches short and sharp: stopping the movement is what makes it look hard
Try punching straight up on the big drops
mistakes: Straightening the arm all the way, which looks floppy and can hurt someone nearby

name: Rave bounce
summary: A light, springy bounce through the balls of the feet, with the chest and shoulders loose.
steps: Weight on the balls of your feet, heels just off the floor
Bounce through the ankles on each beat, knees soft
Let the chest pop forward a little with each bounce
Shoulders loose, hands relaxed at waist height
tips: Keep it small, and it'll last all night
Swap to the knee bounce now and then to rest your calves
mistakes: Jumping off the floor on every beat, which tires you out in one track
why: Rave floors run for hours. A low-effort bounce is what lets you dance from the first track to the last.

name: Running man
counts: Lift on 'and', slide on the beat
summary: Run on the spot: one knee lifts while the standing foot slides back, then they swap.
steps: Stand on your left foot and lift the right knee
On the beat, put the right foot down in front while the left foot slides back
Lift the left knee on the 'and', bringing the foot through
Put it down in front while the right foot slides back, and repeat
tips: Practise in socks on a smooth floor so the slide is easy
Learn it slowly at 100 BPM, then raise the tempo
mistakes: Leaning back: keep the chest a little forward

name: T-step
summary: The standing foot swivels heel-toe to travel sideways while the other leg kicks out.
steps: Stand on your left foot with the right knee lifted
Swivel the left foot: toes out, then heel out, moving you to the left
At the same time, kick the right foot out to the side on each swivel
After four swivels, switch legs and travel the other way
tips: Learn the swivel alone first, holding on to a chair
Smooth floors and trainers help; grippy boots make it hard
mistakes: Travelling too far on a busy floor. Two swivels and back is plenty

name: Arm wave
summary: A ripple that travels from one hand, through the shoulders, to the other hand.
steps: Arms out to the sides at shoulder height
Lift the left wrist, then elbow, then shoulder, one after the other
Pass it across: right shoulder, right elbow, right wrist
Each joint drops as the next one rises
tips: Practise one joint at a time in front of a mirror
Bring it out on the breakdown, when everyone slows down
mistakes: Moving the whole arm at once, so it never ripples
